versions.localizedDescription:
Experimental iOS build with a native mod manager for Sonic (2006) asset overlays. Import extracted mod folders, enable or disable mods, reorder priority, and select built-in codes before playing.

Assets:
- `MarathonRecomp-mods.ipa`: unsigned Release arm64 app, iOS 17+, approximately 44.7 MiB. Sign it before installation.
- SHA-256 checksum, package manifest, validation report and resolved source patch bundle.

Xcode 27.0 compilation and linking succeeded. Mod, portable port, touch/fade and read-only input regressions passed. Package integrity, architecture and absence of signing/provisioning data were checked. Original game files are not included.

This prerelease was built from the local iOS port snapshot on `ios-mod-integration-20261013`; newer changes on `main` are not included. Dev Zero's mod-support authorship is preserved. No device installation or gameplay/performance testing was performed for this build.

apps.name: Mega Man 64
apps.subtitle: Unofficial Mega Man 64 Recompiled mobile port for Android and iOS, with editable touch controls and controller support.
apps.localizedDescription:
Unofficial Mega Man 64 Recompiled mobile port for Android and iOS, with editable touch controls and controller support. Bring your own USA ROM.

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/MegaMan64Recompiled-Mobile

versions.marketingVersion: Mega Man 64 Mobile 0.9.1 — Android and iOS
versions.localizedDescription:
Android and iOS mobile builds of Mega Man 64: Recompiled.

- Editable gameplay and menu touch pads: movement stick, N64 buttons, position/size/opacity/color controls, and GAME PAD / MENU PAD switching.
- SDL USB/Bluetooth controller support and configurable bindings.
- Mobile renderer fixes, Android Vulkan surface/descriptor handling, and iOS screenshot/notification size restoration.
- Persistent USA FlashRAM saves, atomic replacement, backup writes, and background save flushing.
- The supplied Mega Man 64 artwork is now the app icon on both platforms.
- Both application IDs are `com.devz.megaman64`, matching the other ports' naming convention.

**Downloads:** install the ARM64 APK on Android 8.0+ with a compatible Vulkan GPU. Sign the ARM64 IPA for your own iOS 16+ device using eSign or another signing tool. The IPA contains no personal certificate or provisioning profile. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers both downloads.

**ROM:** supply your own Mega Man 64 USA ROM through the launcher. `.z64`, `.v64`, and `.n64` byte orders are accepted. Japanese Rockman DASH gameplay is not supported by this USA recompilation; the loader reports that limitation. No ROM or save data is bundled.

**Existing saves:** the new IDs create separate app storage. Back up the old app's `config/saves` folder before changing builds, preserve filenames, and keep the old app installed until the backup is safe. Storage locations and restoration limits are described in MOBILE.md. Saves are not automatically migrated between different IDs.

The repository starts with a clean source history and pinned dependencies. It excludes ROM-derived generated sources, ROMs, saves, logs, SDKs, local build folders, personal paths, and signing keys. Required build scripts, application assets, licenses, and upstream attribution remain available.

Validation: source privacy and whitespace checks; dependency patches applied against pinned revisions; APK signature and 16 KB alignment; ARM64 package structure; ROM/private-path scans; icon pixel checks, application IDs, Android Java class and all renamed JNI entry points. Rendering/gameplay had been confirmed on iOS and Adreno 710 Android before these icon/ID/publication changes. Installation of this newly packaged release still needs verification on devices.

Upstream: https://github.com/MegaMan64Recomp/MegaMan64Recompiled

apps.name: Super Smash Flash 2
apps.subtitle: Unofficial Super Smash Flash 2 iPhone and iPad port with offline Ruffle runtime, customizable touch controls and gamepad
apps.localizedDescription:
Unofficial Super Smash Flash 2 iPhone and iPad port with offline Ruffle runtime, customizable touch controls and gamepad support.

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/SSF2-iOS

versions.localizedDescription:
Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.6 (build 9) fixes missing audio unlock and an unreliable restart control.

- User taps and key presses explicitly resume the Web Audio contexts used by Ruffle. The custom Play button unlocks audio before starting the game loop.
- Ruffle's unmute overlay is visible as a fallback.
- The native playback audio session is activated and reactivated when appropriate. Headphone disconnection pauses the game; connection, app activation and interruptions are handled.
- The native Restart game button has an explicit layout width and remains enabled while a replacement page loads. Brief duplicate taps are debounced without disabling the control.

A restart creates a new Flash runtime and returns to the title screen. It cannot restore a match from a terminated process. Completed save data and control settings remain in the persistent store. This release does not establish that the earlier memory-related crashes have been eliminated.

Validation: audio unlock, interruption and gesture-retry tests; touch, renderer and cache checks; source/IPA audits; unsigned iOS Release build. The shipped recovery-view component accepted two successive taps in a UIKit Mac Catalyst test app. A native WebKit probe reached a running audio context, but non-silent headphone output still needs verification on affected iPhones.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign it with your sideloading tool. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.5 (build 8) adds native recovery from a failed game page.

- A native Restart game screen handles WebKit process termination, WebGL context loss and sprite-cache read failures. It remains available even when the web controls have disappeared or a failure occurs in the background.
- Restart replaces the WebView, stops the old controller bridge and clears temporary sprite storage. The persistent save-data store remains in use.
- Committed navigation failures are handled as well as provisional failures. Slow restarts allow another attempt after 30 seconds; this does not limit gameplay time.
- Failed sessions require a deliberate restart rather than silently reloading into another failure.

There is no play-time limit. Free storage does not prevent RAM or graphics-memory pressure. This release improves recovery; it does not establish or eliminate every underlying crash. An interrupted match cannot be recovered.

Validation: graphics-loss and cache-read failure notification tests; texture-cache, pixel round-trip, touch and rendering checks; source and IPA audits; unsigned iOS Release build. Native recovery still needs verification on the affected iPhone.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign it with your sideloading tool. Use the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.4 (build 7) reduces memory pressure during startup and character/stage changes.

- Compressed sprites move to temporary native disk storage instead of staying in the JavaScript heap. The WebKit integration test paged approximately 326 MB of compressed sprites to disk.
- Inactive static sprite textures leave a bounded GPU working set and restore through stable logical handles. The target is 128 MB normally, 96 MB on low-memory startup and 64 MB after a memory warning; active draw inputs and modified render targets are preserved.
- Sampler settings, texture-unit bindings and pixel-store state survive restoration.
- Local asset responses use no-store to avoid retaining response bodies in the browser cache.
- The native cache is session-only, reuses freed storage and disappears on app exit.

Keep at least 1 GB of device storage free for normal play; long sessions can require more. If temporary storage cannot be used, compressed sprites fall back to RAM.

Validation: 48-sprite cache stress tests with both RAM and native paging, exact pixel restoration, multiple WebGL contexts, native storage tests, touch/rendering checks, source and IPA audits, and an unsigned iOS Release build. A native macOS WebKit test started a Ness battle, switched to Link and another stage, and reached the next battle without a process termination or sprite-cache read error.

This addresses identified memory pressure, but all crashes on affected iPhones have not yet been verified as resolved. Ruffle can still retain other movie resources.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign it with your sideloading tool. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.3 (build 6) fixes touch layout editing and reduces memory pressure.

- Pause and Start / OK use Space; old Enter pause bindings migrate automatically.
- MENU replaces the Escape-based Back button and opens the app control panel.
- D-pad dragging supports upward movement, pointer capture, resizing and reset.
- Fullscreen landscape play is enabled by default, with overlay controls.
- Deferred textures release their original pixel buffers; upload buffers are reused and rendering resolution is capped.
- Memory warnings or WebKit process termination enable persistent lower-memory rendering, with a controlled retry after repeated failure.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign and install it with your preferred sideloading tool. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Validation: JavaScript control, memory-retention and rendering tests; source and IPA privacy audits; unsigned iOS Release build. Simultaneous-KO crashes still need testing on physical iPhones; the memory fixes cannot guarantee every device avoids iOS memory limits.

First public release of the Super Smash Flash 2 iPhone and iPad port.

- Offline Super Smash Flash 2 v1.3.1.2 Portable, with bundled Ruffle 0.6.0.
- Matching multitouch control deck, adjustable size and opacity, and separate customizable portrait/landscape layouts.
- Native gamepad support and remappable touch, keyboard, and controller actions.
- Deferred compressed texture uploads to reduce GPU memory use.
- Clean public source with checksum-pinned asset downloads and reproducible unsigned IPA packaging.
- Release builds exclude the device test command channel, diagnostic files, source maps, signing files, and embedded local build paths.

**Installation:** Requires iOS/iPadOS 16 or later. Download the unsigned IPA, sign it with your preferred sideloading tool, and install. Preserve the bundle identifier and signing identity when updating to keep app data.

The game runs offline; online multiplayer is unsupported. Performance and Flash compatibility depend on the device and Ruffle.

**Validation:** Xcode Release build, touch/controller/layout tests, texture memory tests, source privacy audit, and final IPA integrity/privacy audit passed. The SHA-256 checksum is attached.

See the README for controls, installation, building, credits, and licenses.

apps.name: Slam’n’Jam 96
apps.subtitle: Native iOS and Windows ports of SSF2T, UMK3, Slam 'n Jam 96 and THPS2
apps.localizedDescription:
Native iOS and Windows ports of SSF2T, UMK3, Slam 'n Jam 96 and THPS2

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/NativePorts

versions.marketingVersion: NativePorts 0.2.2 — SSF2T and Slam n Jam fixes
versions.localizedDescription:
SSF2T and Slam n Jam 0.2.2

iOS and Windows builds passed. iOS IPAs are unsigned; sign/install with ESign, keeping the existing bundle identifiers.

Slam n Jam: startup asks for keyboard 1 or controller Start, with no coin prompt. Restart reads RESTART GAME. PS1 Select is available as Select (keyboard Tab, controller View); old settings migrate. Native gameplay canvas expands from 320 to 426 columns instead of stretching. Original-size sprites, text and HUD remain centered; textures live in original VRAM and expanded framebuffers use separate banks. CRT behavior is unchanged.

SSF2T: reflected edge artwork removed. The visible gameplay window narrows symmetrically as the camera approaches finite stage boundaries, returning to the original 384 columns at either limit. It expands away from those limits. Menus keep their original proportions centered in a 512-column frame with colored sides.

Validation: iOS and Windows builds, controller suite, canvas isolation and stage-boundary tests passed. Real Slam gameplay toggled 320 -> 426 -> 320 columns; all 81,920 pixels of the central original view matched the same saved frame exactly. Real SSF2T gameplay captures returned to 384 columns at both edges, and menu captures were 512 columns with colored margins. Device-specific iPhone and Windows gameplay still needs retesting.

No game files or game screenshots are included. This release updates SSF2T and Slam n Jam only. THPS2 and UMK3 remain available in release 0.2.1.

THPS2 now has a direct CRT ON/OFF button during iPhone gameplay, black top/bottom letterbox bars on iOS and Windows, and a renderer adjustment to keep flat HUD overlays in the central 4:3 area. The iOS CPU interpreter also has a faster RAM instruction-fetch path.

Slam ’n Jam widescreen projection now runs before guest clipping and preserves native sprite/text rendering. SSF2T extends finite scenery edges with mirrored backgrounds while preserving sprite priority. UMK3 extends mixed background tile bands with safeguards for unrelated props.

### Downloads

- Four unsigned iOS IPAs: sign and install using ESign.
- Windows x64 ZIP: contains all four games and required SDL libraries.
- SHA256SUMS.txt: checksums for the downloadable builds.

Existing bundle identifiers are preserved. Game files are not included. NBA Showtime remains unfinished and is not included.

### Validation and remaining checks

All four iOS and Windows builds passed. Controller, VRAM, GTE projection and stage-edge regression checks passed; 92 Dreamcast shader variants compiled and linked. A local Slam ’n Jam gameplay capture showed complete crowd rendering in one tested camera.

THPS2 iPhone frame-rate improvement and HUD placement still need device confirmation. Slam ’n Jam shot-clock readability and other cameras, plus affected SSF2T and UMK3 stages, still need gameplay retesting. Native PS1 resolution is unchanged. SSF2T edge scenery uses reflected existing artwork.

NativePorts 0.2.0 includes Super Street Fighter II Turbo, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3, Slam ’n Jam ’96 and Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2 for iOS and Windows.

- Uses the supplied game artwork for each iOS app and Windows executable/window icon. Keeps unique bundle IDs unchanged to preserve installed game data.
- Adds game-specific widescreen patches for SSF2T, UMK3 and Slam ’n Jam ’96, alongside the existing Flycast widescreen patch for THPS2. Widescreen can be toggled in display settings.
- Updates aspect-ratio handling and NewPixie CRT rendering to preserve picture edges. CRT filtering remains enabled by default and can be disabled.
- Refreshes cached core sources before builds so source changes rebuild the embedded engine.
- Includes touch controls and remappable multiplayer controller support on both platforms.

Download one unsigned IPA per game and sign it with your sideloading tool. For Windows, extract NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip and keep each EXE beside its SDL2.dll. Use your own game files; ROMs, disc images and signing credentials are not included.

Known limitations: THPS2 on iOS uses an interpreter and may run below full speed. Slam ’n Jam ’96 can leave dark corners in some widescreen camera angles. NBA Showtime remains frontend-only and is not included.

Validation: all four iOS build logs report success; Windows binaries were packaged from the latest local builds. Virtual controller tests passed for all five frontends, along with ROM-import checks, basketball action tests and both THPS2 texture-cache configurations. These checks do not establish full-speed performance or physical multiplayer operation on every device. SHA256SUMS.txt contains asset checksums.

Super Street Fighter II Turbo 0.1.1, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 0.1.1, Slam 'n Jam '96 0.1.1 and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 0.1.9 for iOS and Windows. Unsigned IPAs for sideloading (ESign, AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly) and a Windows x64 package. No game files are included; see the README for what you need.

apps.localizedDescription:
NBA Hangtime (Midway arcade, 1996) for iPhone, iPad and Windows: true widescreen, big head modes, touch and Xbox/PlayStation controller support. Bring your own ROMs.

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/NBAHangtime-iOS

versions.localizedDescription:
# NBA Hangtime 0.4.4

iOS build 9 · Windows x64 · iOS 16 or later

## Changes

- Match CRT curvature to the corrected ports: CURVATURE 1.0 with a 40% blend toward the flat image.
- Remove frame-artwork overscan and prevent outermost pixels from smearing beyond the curved screen.
- Fade the tube boundary into black with a 1.5-pixel edge mask.
- Generate the iOS and Windows CRT shaders from the same math.

## Downloads

- `NBA-Hangtime-iOS.ipa` — unsigned; sign with your sideloading tool.
- `NBA-Hangtime-Windows-x64.zip`
- `NBA-Hangtime-0.4.4-source.zip` — matching port and patched core source.

Companion SHA-256 checksums are included. Game ROMs are not included; the complete L1.1 arcade set is required. See `SOURCE.md` for source and license notices.

## Validation

Geometry regression checks cover the curvature values, symmetry, all four borders and edge fade. Windows and iOS release builds passed. OpenGL and Metal GPU tests passed shader compilation, rendering passes, black corners, image orientation, toggles and resizing. Package integrity and privacy checks passed before publication.

GPU tests ran on the Mac host. Visual confirmation on physical iOS and Windows devices remains pending.

# NBA Hangtime 0.4.3

iOS build 8 · Windows x64 · iOS 16 or later

## New in 0.4.3

- Add the NewPixie CRT filter on iOS and Windows. Enable or disable CRT FILTER from the iOS Display menu or Windows pause menu.
- Save the setting across launches; default to OFF. Apply changes immediately without restarting the game.
- Preserve the original pixel display with CRT off, and reset feedback when toggling or switching widescreen frame sizes.

## Changes since 0.4.0

- Fix Windows Xbox input by reading buttons, sticks and triggers through XInput. Gameplay, controller setup and menus use the same polled input state.
- Improve iOS controller event delivery, including Menu/Start and gamepad routing on iOS 18 and later.
- Keep controller slots stable across reordering and disconnects. Controllers join as Player 1, Player 3, Player 2 and Player 4.
- Align Player 1 and Player 4 possession indicators and scoring flashes with their status plates.
- Restore camera tracking at both near-side corners. Limit the inbound view separately so it stays inside the available scenery at both court ends.
- Preserve live settings changes, including switching head size during gameplay. Normal, big and huge head settings apply to all four players.
- Strip private build paths and debug metadata from release binaries. Check packages for ROMs, signing credentials and development artifacts.
- Include license notices and matching source references in both binary packages.

## Downloads

# Sonic Unleashed for iOS v1.1.0 — Native Mod Manager

## Changelog

- Added a native startup mod manager with folder import through Files.
- Enable or disable mods, reorder priority, and preserve selections across launches.
- Check dependency IDs and minimum numeric versions before starting.
- Toggle the built-in game codes from the manager.
- Connect selections to the existing asset replacements, append archives, loose files, UMM merges, and mod save redirection.
- Display unsupported DLL and custom HMM script requirements.
- Confine mod include/save paths and reject symbolic links.
- Compile the game Metal shader cache for iOS 15 with the iPhone SDK.
- Target iOS 15 for bundled dependencies and use numeric bundle versions.
- Add an IPA packaging helper for builds made with the Ninja preset.

## Install and use

Download `SonicUnleashed_iOS_v1.1.0.ipa` and re-sign it with your sideloading tool before installation. This IPA has an ad-hoc signature and no Apple provisioning profile. Supply your own runtime game assets through Files.

Extract an Unleashed Recompiled mod, launch the app, tap **Import folder**, and select the folder containing `mod.ini`. Enable it, set its priority, and tap **Play**. New imports start disabled. The first mod wins file replacement conflicts.

## Compatibility and validation

ARM64 iPhone/iPad build targeting iOS 15 or later. DLL plugins and arbitrary HMM scripts need individual iOS ports; this release does not promise compatibility with every mod. There is no online mod catalog or automatic downloading.

The complete app compiled and linked successfully. Mod backend tests passed with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, and the native UI passed ARM64 iOS SDK syntax checks. The packaged IPA passed ZIP integrity, bundle metadata, and ad-hoc signature checks. Physical-device gameplay and individual mod packages have not been verified.

Source: `5625afe81d2f9f2bac947087034260dc8c87dcc1`.
First release

apps.subtitle: Native iOS and Windows ports of SSF2T, UMK3, Slam 'n Jam 96 and THPS2

Native iOS and Windows ports of SSF2T, UMK3, Slam 'n Jam 96 and THPS2

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/NativePorts

versions.localizedDescription:
THPS2 now has a direct CRT ON/OFF button during iPhone gameplay, black top/bottom letterbox bars on iOS and Windows, and a renderer adjustment to keep flat HUD overlays in the central 4:3 area. The iOS CPU interpreter also has a faster RAM instruction-fetch path.

Slam ’n Jam widescreen projection now runs before guest clipping and preserves native sprite/text rendering. SSF2T extends finite scenery edges with mirrored backgrounds while preserving sprite priority. UMK3 extends mixed background tile bands with safeguards for unrelated props.

### Downloads

- Four unsigned iOS IPAs: sign and install using ESign.
- Windows x64 ZIP: contains all four games and required SDL libraries.
- SHA256SUMS.txt: checksums for the downloadable builds.

Existing bundle identifiers are preserved. Game files are not included. NBA Showtime remains unfinished and is not included.

### Validation and remaining checks

All four iOS and Windows builds passed. Controller, VRAM, GTE projection and stage-edge regression checks passed; 92 Dreamcast shader variants compiled and linked. A local Slam ’n Jam gameplay capture showed complete crowd rendering in one tested camera.

THPS2 iPhone frame-rate improvement and HUD placement still need device confirmation. Slam ’n Jam shot-clock readability and other cameras, plus affected SSF2T and UMK3 stages, still need gameplay retesting. Native PS1 resolution is unchanged. SSF2T edge scenery uses reflected existing artwork.

NativePorts 0.2.0 includes Super Street Fighter II Turbo, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3, Slam ’n Jam ’96 and Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2 for iOS and Windows.

- Uses the supplied game artwork for each iOS app and Windows executable/window icon. Keeps unique bundle IDs unchanged to preserve installed game data.
- Adds game-specific widescreen patches for SSF2T, UMK3 and Slam ’n Jam ’96, alongside the existing Flycast widescreen patch for THPS2. Widescreen can be toggled in display settings.
- Updates aspect-ratio handling and NewPixie CRT rendering to preserve picture edges. CRT filtering remains enabled by default and can be disabled.
- Refreshes cached core sources before builds so source changes rebuild the embedded engine.
- Includes touch controls and remappable multiplayer controller support on both platforms.

Download one unsigned IPA per game and sign it with your sideloading tool. For Windows, extract NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip and keep each EXE beside its SDL2.dll. Use your own game files; ROMs, disc images and signing credentials are not included.

Known limitations: THPS2 on iOS uses an interpreter and may run below full speed. Slam ’n Jam ’96 can leave dark corners in some widescreen camera angles. NBA Showtime remains frontend-only and is not included.

Validation: all four iOS build logs report success; Windows binaries were packaged from the latest local builds. Virtual controller tests passed for all five frontends, along with ROM-import checks, basketball action tests and both THPS2 texture-cache configurations. These checks do not establish full-speed performance or physical multiplayer operation on every device. SHA256SUMS.txt contains asset checksums.

Super Street Fighter II Turbo 0.1.1, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 0.1.1, Slam 'n Jam '96 0.1.1 and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 0.1.9 for iOS and Windows. Unsigned IPAs for sideloading (ESign, AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly) and a Windows x64 package. No game files are included; see the README for what you need.

versions.localizedDescription:
# Changelog

## 1.0.0 (build 3)

First release.

- SEGA Superstars Tennis (Xbox 360) on iPhone and iPad, recompiled with the iOS port of ReXGlue and drawn through Vulkan on Metal (MoltenVK). iOS 15 or later.
- Direct Xbox 360 ISO/XISO loading with **Choose ISO**, or extracted disc files in the app's `game` folder.
- Matches at up to 60 FPS, capped at 60. CPU readback of the shaders' memory exports is off by default: it made the GPU thread wait for the GPU 30-50 times a frame (12-14 FPS in a match on an iPhone 14 Pro Max).
- The game's busy waits (Direct3D's wait for the GPU, the audio threads' barrier) sleep briefly instead of spinning a core, which keeps the phone cooler during long sessions.
- The picture stays landscape and sharp after Notification Center, Control Center, screenshots and app switches. iOS lays the window out in portrait for its background snapshot, and the swap chain used to stay portrait afterwards.
- On-screen touch controls when no controller is connected; MFi, Xbox and PlayStation controllers.
- Pause and resume on app switches and locking; game language from the device; shader and pipeline caches kept across launches; Apple Game Mode.

versions.localizedDescription:
## MCX360 Edition 1.1

### New
- **On-screen touch controls**, using the layout from the XeniOS emulator. They show when no controller is connected and hide when one connects. Adjust them with `touch_controls`, `touch_controls_opacity` and `touch_haptics` in `mc360.toml`.
- **Save thumbnails**: your worlds now show a picture in the world list.
- **Exit Game** now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen.

### Performance
- Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds.
- Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (`framerate_limit`, default 60).
- The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores.
- Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame.

### Fixes
- Fixed random crashes after playing for a while.
- Fixed choppy audio.
- Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed.
- Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing.

### Known issues
- Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps.
- The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save.
- Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement.

Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.
First iOS release.
